headline: Low prompt-injection and data-leakage risk; no documented shared channel, but Rasa can ingest external messages while RisingWave is read-only here.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Rasa ingests messages from external chat channels by default, so attacker-controlled text could reach its dialogue logic. RisingWave exposes no input channel or instruction parser in the profile, so the pairwise bridge is indirect and likely manual rather than automatic. No shared filesystem or MCP bridge is documented, so this stays low, not medium.
conditions: IF Rasa is connected to a user-controlled chat channel that forwards raw text into dialogue handling
IF an operator copies Rasa output into a downstream prompt or parser without sanitization
mitigations: Restrict Rasa to trusted channels only
Add a prompt-injection filter on inbound messages
Disable any auto-forwarding from Rasa to other agents
Review a sample of live messages for instruction-like payloads
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Rasa touches text and voice and can egress to allowlisted services, while RisingWave shows no data classes touched and no egress. The profiles do not document a shared workspace, shared OAuth principal, or file exchange, so leakage is not evidenced beyond a narrow messaging path. Because the interaction is undocumented, uncertainty keeps this at low rather than none.
conditions: IF Rasa is configured to forward transcripts or voice-derived text into RisingWave inputs
IF both agents are granted access to the same sensitive message store
mitigations: Limit Rasa transcripts to non-sensitive fields
Separate credentials for each agent
Turn off transcript forwarding unless needed
Check logs for accidental payload sharing
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Rasa is not runnable and supports no multiple instances, while RisingWave has no write or concurrency surfaces documented. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely in the profiles provided. Because no shared mutable resource is described, the remaining risk is only a weak coordination mismatch, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same mutable resource
IF Rasa is wrapped in a custom deployment that bypasses its single-instance constraint
mitigations: Assign separate storage paths
Avoid concurrent writes to shared tables
Serialize any handoff between agents
Document ownership of mutable resources
requires-engineering: add locking around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Rasa can produce conversational outputs that may be treated as authoritative by downstream systems, while RisingWave is a data-engineering component that could consume those outputs if wired in. The profiles do not show verification gates or provenance checks, so an output-to-input chain is plausible in default integrations. The blast radius is multiple work products, not just one document.
conditions: IF RisingWave ingests Rasa-generated text as operational input without validation
IF downstream jobs act on Rasa outputs as facts rather than suggestions
mitigations: Add schema validation before ingestion
Require human review for high-impact actions
Log source provenance on every handoff
Reject low-confidence Rasa outputs
requires-engineering: implement verification checkpoints

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either agent. Rasa is open-source customer-support software and RisingWave is open-source data-engineering software, but the profiles do not show PHI, EU PII, or conflicting compliance regimes. With no compliance-specific evidence, a breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF either deployment is later configured to process regulated data under conflicting policies
mitigations: Document the data classes in scope
Confirm retention settings before deployment
Review residency requirements for any regulated data
Keep regulated workloads out of this pair
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement controls
